Package neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline

Class TwoFluidConservativeEnergyReport

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.TwoFluidConservativeEnergyReport
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class TwoFluidConservativeEnergyReport extends Object implements Serializable
Accepted fluid total-energy accounting for the opt-in conservative thermodynamic recovery route.

Stored energy includes phase internal and kinetic energy, with the equation of state's caloric reference. Positive advected energy, gravitational work and wall heat add energy to the fluid. Advected energy includes the accepted pressure-correction face transfers. Wall heat includes any direct electrical heating deposited in the fluid; wall storage and ambient exchange are outside this fluid control volume. Neither Joule-Thomson nor latent heat is an independent energy source when phase enthalpies and internal energies already represent these effects.

This discrete ledger and its independent published-state residuals establish numerical consistency for the accepted interval. They do not establish experimental qualification of the phase-transfer or hydrodynamic closures.

1.0

Even Solbraa

      public TwoFluidConservativeEnergyReport(double elapsedTimeSeconds, double initialEnergyJ, double finalEnergyJ, double netAdvectedEnergyJ, double gravitationalWorkJ, double wallHeatToFluidJ, double maxRelativeVolumeResidual, double maxRelativeThermodynamicEnergyResidual)

      finalEnergyJ - final integrated internal plus kinetic energy in joules

      wallHeatToFluidJ - integrated heat added to the fluid, including electrical heating, in joules

    • TwoFluidConservativeEnergyReport

      public TwoFluidConservativeEnergyReport(double elapsedTimeSeconds, double initialEnergyJ, double finalEnergyJ, double inletAdvectedEnergyJ, double outletAdvectedEnergyJ, double gravitationalWorkJ, double wallHeatToFluidJ, double maxRelativeVolumeResidual, double maxRelativeThermodynamicEnergyResidual)
      Construct an accepted-interval fluid energy ledger with boundary-resolved advection.

      Boundary transfers retain their finite-volume sign convention: positive inlet energy enters from the upstream boundary and positive outlet energy leaves through the downstream boundary. Their difference is the net advected energy added to the pipe. Keeping the two transfers separate allows a network junction to route the exact accepted branch energy without reconstructing it from an end state.

      Parameters:
      elapsedTimeSeconds - accepted elapsed time in seconds
      initialEnergyJ - initial integrated internal plus kinetic energy in joules
      finalEnergyJ - final integrated internal plus kinetic energy in joules
      inletAdvectedEnergyJ - signed accepted energy through the inlet face in joules
      outletAdvectedEnergyJ - signed accepted energy through the outlet face in joules
      gravitationalWorkJ - integrated gravitational work on the fluid in joules
      wallHeatToFluidJ - integrated heat added to the fluid, including electrical heating, in joules
      maxRelativeVolumeResidual - maximum absolute occupied-volume residual relative to cell volume
      maxRelativeThermodynamicEnergyResidual - maximum absolute discrepancy between conservative and reconstructed thermodynamic total energy, relative to the recovery solver's energy scale
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a quantity is nonfinite or a time/residual is negative
